chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban, from Isma'il al-Ju'fi, who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'The best making up of voluntary prayers is making up the night prayer at night and the day prayer during the day.' I said: 'So there will be two Witr prayers in one night?' He said: 'No.' I said: 'And why do you command me to perform two Witr prayers in one night?' He said (peace be upon him): 'One of them is a making up (qada).'
ai.seo_question: What is the best time to make up missed voluntary night prayers according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) establishes the principle of temporal fidelity in making up missed voluntary prayers, ensuring that the night prayer (Salat al-Layl) is performed at night and the day prayer during the day. He clarifies a common jurisprudential query regarding whether this results in two Witr prayers in a single night, ruling that one serves as the makeup (Qada) while the other remains the current night's Witr, thereby preserving the distinct spiritual status of each obligation.
